keyVerseText: And it shall come to pass, while my glory passeth by, that I will put thee in a clift of the rock, and will cover thee with my hand while I pass by:
rootMeaning: The root of נְקָרָה (nᵉqârâh) is נָקַר (nâqar), which conveys the action of digging, piercing, or boring into a substance. This root emphasizes the idea of creating a fissure or opening by penetrating or quarrying, rather than merely a passive crack. Thus, נְקָרָה carries the sense of a deliberate hollow or cleft formed by an active process of excavation, highlighting a tangible, physical indentation or crevice beyond the abstract notion of a hole.
usageInScripture: This word appears only twice in Scripture, consistently translated to reflect a natural cleft or opening in rock or stone, such as 'thee in a clift' and 'into the clefts.' The limited occurrences reveal a focused semantic range emphasizing a physical refuge or hollow space, often associated with protection or concealment. The translations underscore the tangible and protective nature of these fissures, showing the word’s use in describing natural features that serve a divine or practical purpose.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding נְקָרָה as a cleft or hollow formed by piercing deepens our appreciation of God’s provision of refuge in Scripture. It symbolizes not just any shelter but one carved out by force or design, mirroring how God actively shapes circumstances to protect His people. This word enriches the biblical portrayal of God as a refuge who makes a safe place amid danger, reflecting His sovereign power to create security through His glory. For the Christian faith, it reminds believers of the intimate and tangible ways God shelters His people, not abstractly but in a deeply personal and protective manner.
keyVerseReflection: In Exodus 33:22, God promises to place Moses 'in a clift of the rock' while His glory passes by, using נְקָרָה to describe this cleft. This word conveys the image of a deep, secure crevice carved into the rock where Moses is hidden and shielded by God's hand. It highlights the protective intimacy of God's presence, showing that He provides a tangible, carved-out refuge for His servant to safely witness His glory without harm.
